newsitem.title: UK: Sterling slide baffles British bureaux de change.
newsitem.headline: Sterling slide baffles British bureaux de change.

text.p: The speed of sterling's dramatic slide during the European morning session on Thursday was indicated graphically by the inability of high street bureaux de change to keep up with the decline.
"I'm standing outside a bureau de change in Oxford Street (London) and sterling is quoted at 2.5427 (marks) bid," one lunching foreign exchange trader told Reuters via his mobile phone.
At the same time, sterling was trading in the interbank market at 2.5325/35 marks.
"So you can get a better price for sterling in Oxford Street than you can on the interbank market," the trader said.
It was the same with sterling/dollar, which was bid at $1.63 versus $1.62 interbank and sterling/French franc which was bid at 8.5720 against the market price of 8.5510.
Typically, prices for the public in the high street are quoted with a massive spread which straddles the interbank bid and offer by several German pfennigs.
In the past 72 hours, sterling has lost as much as 12 pfennigs or 4.5 percent of its value since early Tuesday.
